1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with generous spacing around headings, labels, fields, and buttons.

2.why: Instructions are short sentence-case lines with no italics, all-caps, or dense paragraphs; the only uppercase string is the setup secret itself, not instruction text.

3.why: The screenshots are desktop-width showing a centered single-column card, so rendering at a mobile screen size cannot be confirmed, though the simple layout appears reflow-friendly.

4.why: Each screen carries one short instruction such as 'Enter your registered details to begin MFA enrolment,' though terms like 'MFA enrolment' and 'authenticator' are mild jargon.

5.why: The six-digit code field has no placeholder or worked example of the expected input; only the pre-filled login fields show any format.

6.why: No screen contains more than two short lines of text, so no long block must be read to proceed.

7.why: The 32-character secret is displayed as plain text with no copy button, so copying via text selection may be possible but cannot be confirmed from the screenshots.

8.why: No QR code or any alternative to manual entry is offered; the screen explicitly instructs 'Choose manual entry and enter this setup secret.'

9.why: There is no password field and no visible evidence of autocomplete or one-time-code support, so autofill and password-manager support can neither be confirmed nor denied.

10.why: Each screen has a bold descriptive heading and one prominent solid-blue primary button, but there is no explicit step indicator such as 'Step 2 of 3.'

11.why: Every screen asks for exactly one main action ('Verify and continue', 'Set up authenticator app', 'Confirm code'), with only a visually de-emphasised 'Log out' alongside.

12.why: After verification the UI advances without plainly confirming what happened (status appears only in the test Logs panel), and the failure message 'We could not complete that request' does not state what occurred or what comes next.

13.why: After a wrong code the screen invites 'Please try again' with the form intact and no lockout or penalty shown, though no re-request or regenerate control is visible.

14.why: The only error shown, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again,' does not blame the user but fails to state the actual problem (wrong or expired code) or how to fix it.

15.why: No countdown or reading time limit is visible anywhere, but the on-screen note that the code is 'time-bound' confirms codes expire, so entry time is inherently limited.
